questions.stem: At very high temperatures, transpiration rate may actually decrease. Why?

options.text: Water freezes inside the xylem vessels
The plant's stomata may close to prevent excessive water loss and wilting
Photosynthesis stops, so the plant no longer needs CO2
The air becomes too dry for water to evaporate

questions.explanation: At very high temperatures, the plant risks losing too much water and wilting. To prevent this, the stomata close, which reduces water loss but also limits gas exchange for photosynthesis.
